findings.summary: `var pingTimer;` is declared but the `setInterval(...)` call on the next line is never assigned to it (should be `pingTimer=setInterval(...)`). The onclose handler at line 876 calls `clearInterval(pingTimer)`, but pingTimer is always undefined, so that call is a permanent no-op. Since the socket auto-reconnects ~3s after any drop (per the existing onclose/setTimeout(connect,...) logic), every reconnect's `connect()` invocation starts a brand-new 15s interval that is never cleared — exactly the 'ping timer from a previous connection torn down... so reconnecting doesn't leave multiple ping loops running concurrently' failure mode the brief explicitly calls out to prevent. Verified server-side support already exists (src/dashboard/site-live.ts:310-315 webSocketMessage handles 'ping' by recomputing and returning currentSnapshot()), so the only gap is this client-side teardown bug.

findings.summary: The new test only checks that the literal substring "clearInterval(pingTimer)" appears in the rendered script text; it never executes the script or simulates a reconnect, so it passes identically whether or not pingTimer is ever assigned. It does not actually verify the anti-leak behavior it was written to cover (per its own inline comment) and did not catch the Critical bug above despite the implementer's report that tests were written and run for this change.
